subject: Post-call recap: Bakeoff criteria & next tests (Redwood vs Nimbus)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Bakeoff criteria & next tests (Redwood vs Nimbus)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the hands-on tests next week. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak hourly concurrency (esp. end-of-day batch ingestion)
- Token-unit cost is ballooning due to lack of shared KV caching across requests
- Need deterministic inference behavior for compliance (reproducible prompts + version pinning)

Primary goals for the bakeoff:
1) Meet 99th-percentile latency target <= 450ms for interactive flows at 100 concurrent sessions
2) Reduce per-token cost by at least 25% versus current baseline through batching/caching/quantization where possible
3) Verify auditability: request-level logs, model versioning, and exportable KV cache events

Decision criteria (what Finex will score):
- Performance (P95/P99) on your representative workload
- Cost per 1k tokens under scaled test runs (hourly and sustained)
- Observability / traceability feature set (logs, traces, token attribution)
- Ease of integration and rollout risk (SDKs, canary strategy)

Agreed technical tests and owners:
- Data & dataset: Finex will provide a 10k-line sample prompt set + synthetic concurrency harness. (Alex to share via Drive)
- Live throughput test: Redwood will run 2 x 1-hour runs at 100 and 250 concurrent sessions (Marcus lead)
- Tail latency stress: Redwood will run a spike test with bursty traffic and measure P99 (Aditya lead)
- Cost simulation: Redwood will provide per-token cost modeling using your traffic profile

Attachments sent with this email:
- Bakeoff_Scorecard_v1.xlsx (scorecard template we’ll use for scoring)
- redwood-vs-nimbus-kpi-matrix.pdf (initial comparison; vendor self-reported metrics)

Proposed schedule (please confirm):
- Thu Jul 9 morning (Finex time): share dataset and expected SLAs (Alex)
- Mon Jul 13: Redwood runs first live throughput test (Marcus)
- Tue Jul 14: Tail latency stress test + cost simulation (Aditya)
- Fri Jul 17: Joint readout and scorecard review

Open questions we still have:
- Is the sample dataset allowed to include PII? If not, please indicate which fields must be redacted.
- Any hard blocker compliance rules (retention <-> audit export windows) we should know about up front?

Next steps / asks for Finex:
1) Share dataset link + any redaction constraints by EOD Thu Jul 9
2) Confirm preferred time window on Mon Jul 13 for the first run (we can do 08:00–12:00 PT or 13:00–17:00 PT)
3) Signed mutual NDA for the test artifacts if you want logs exported — DocSend link below for convenience

DocSend: https://docsend.com/view/finex-bakeoff-nda
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/finex/1234567

Thanks — looking forward to the tests.

—
